bugs.title: Order and history calls time out 25-30 s after 5-minute candle closes
bugs.impact: Order timeouts drive every bookkeeping bug above; a 20-minute positionbook outage on 10-28 left the engine blind.
evidence: 10-30: 12 Timeout sending order at 10:15, 10:25, 10:40, 11:15
execution-health: Timeout sending order x12, slow sandbox place_order above 5 s x10, limiter critical-lane max wait 13.4 s, refused calls 1447

Reopen criteria from the Phase B verification met on 2026-11-04: 34 'Timeout sending order' (first 10:00:58, last 14:45:26; AXISBANK x6, COALINDIA x3, others) and 38 core 'Slow sandbox place_order' calls above 20 s of 61 logged (48 above 5 s, 43 above 15 s), longest 354,210 ms (CGPOWER 15:15:43), then 336,951 ms (RELIANCE 15:00:54), 268,422 ms (LAURUSLABS 15:09:03), 264,432 ms (SHRIRAMFIN 14:10:03). In every one the price stage dominates (e.g. 353,913 of 354,210 ms) and execute is under 600 ms: the quote lookup inside place_order stalls, it is not the sandbox fill lock. The 20 s order_timeout covers neither. The 2 and 3 Nov verification (max 12.5 s, 0 timeouts) still describes those two days.
bugs.root_cause: Two separate causes. (A) 2026-10-30: sandbox fills serialised under ExecutionEngine._position_lock (fixed by the 20 s order_timeout; verified 11-02, 11-03). (B) 2026-11-04: the Flattrade GetQuotes call inside sandbox place_order hangs. Of 61 slow place_order calls the price stage was 99% of the time in every one (max 353,913 of 354,210 ms), execute under 600 ms. The shared HTTP client waits up to 120 s per call (utils/httpx_client.py REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and broker/flattrade/api/data.py:167 retries once, which fits 354 s. The Flattrade limiter's own latency_max reached 744 s from about 12:00 and 120 of 372 summaries show max over 20 s; the critical lane waited at most 32.5 s, so it is not our limiter queue. 20 s order_timeout cannot cover this. Mitigation options that change execution semantics and need owner approval: a short timeout with no retry for quote reads made inside place_order, or pricing a sandbox MARKET exit from the engine's own last tick.
bugs.fix: signal_engine: placeorder uses api.order_timeout 20 s (other calls stay 5 s), covering the measured burst; genuine timeouts still reconcile and watch for late fills. Test: test_order_timeout.py. The sandbox lock itself is not changed: b6887f319 logs the time inside the lock per fill, needed before narrowing it.
bugs.verification: 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03 (Phase B review): the same metric before and after. 10-30: 10 sandbox place_order calls over 5 s and 12 'Timeout sending order'. 11-02: 10 calls over 5 s (max 12.5 s) and 0 timeouts; 11-03: 2 calls over 5 s (max 11.7 s) and 0 timeouts. All 12 were traced in the engine log: each got an order id and a fill, none EXIT UNCERTAIN, none >20 s. Bursts: 11-02 10:20:50-52 three exits at 5.7/6.4/7.6 s all booked; cycles with 4+ submitted: 11-02 09:50 (5), 11-03 09:45 (5), 09:50 (5), 09:55 (4). bugs.title: Scheduled-jobs check turns every RED morning into a failed job, so open-day stays RED each day
bugs.plain: The morning readiness check shows RED every day even when the stack is fine, because it counts yesterday's own RED result as a failed job. A real alert would be buried in the noise.
bugs.impact: open-day reports RED (and sends a Telegram alert) every trading day since 2 Nov with no real fault; a genuine RED is indistinguishable. Also the Windows task check cannot run from cron.
evidence: close-day status tsv: jobs exit 1 on 2026-10-30 (manual 17:34 re-run), 2026-11-02, 2026-11-03. jobs-2026-11-02/03.json: only FAIL is 'phase open-day: check exit 1'. open-day-2026-11-02/03/04.json: only FAIL is 'close-day <prev>: failed steps [jobs]'. All other 12 open-day checks OK on 11-04.
bugs.root_cause: Two parts. (1) Loop: ops step exit 1 means 'verdict RED', but jobs._phase_checks and readiness._yesterday_close read any nonzero step exit as 'job failed/did not run'. A RED open-day makes that day's jobs RED (exit 1), which makes the next open-day RED, indefinitely. (2) schtasks.exe is called by bare name (jobs.py:48, readiness.py:193); it is not on PATH under cron or the agent shell, but /mnt/c/Windows/System32/schtasks.exe works, so the Windows task audit is always NOT VERIFIED.
bugs.fix: signal_engine/ops/jobs.py: schtasks_exe() resolves PATH then /mnt/c/Windows/System32/schtasks.exe; reported_red() treats a step that exited 1 with its own fresh RED report as ran-and-reported (WARN), while other exit codes, a missing report or a report older than the run stay FAIL. readiness.py uses both (schtasks path, _yesterday_close). 4 regression tests in signal_engine/tests/test_ops_phases.py (11 pass). Uncommitted. Pre-change 11-04 open-day report backed up at ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/bug013/.

bugs.title: Readiness check reports a healthy OpenAlgo as 'not answering' when its health status is warn
bugs.plain: The morning readiness check calls OpenAlgo 'not answering' whenever its health status is a warning, even though it is answering normally. That raises a false RED for a problem that does not exist.
bugs.impact: An open-day run after about 09:30 IST reports FAIL and RED for a server that returns HTTP 200. The 09:12 cron run passes only because the thread count has not yet risen. A real outage is hidden among false alarms.
evidence: signal_engine/ops/readiness.py:66 maps any status other than 'pass' to FAIL. 2026-11-04 13:10 open-day re-run: 'OpenAlgo health: http://127.0.0.1:5000/health/status status=warn' FAIL while curl returned HTTP 200. db/health.db latest row: thread_count=70, thread_status=warn, every other component pass. Warn samples on every trading day 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-04.
bugs.root_cause: readiness._health returns OK only for 'pass' and FAIL for everything else. The endpoint's contract (blueprints/health.py) is pass, warn, fail, with HTTP 503 only on fail. Expected mapping: pass to OK, warn to WARN, fail or HTTP 503 or unreachable to FAIL. The warn itself is the thread count above its 50 threshold (a separate matter, not part of this entry).

bugs.title: Scheduler auto-login logs a cache-notification error on every master contract download and skips the Python strategy restore
bugs.plain: Every automatic morning login logs two false errors after the symbols load correctly. They make the end-of-day report show a FAIL for application errors every day, and they hide any real error. No trade was affected.
bugs.impact: The EOD check 'OpenAlgo app errors today' FAILs daily (49 errors on 2026-11-03) and open-day shows a WARN, both from this one cause, so a real app error is buried. In the scheduler process the post-login Python strategy restore never runs; on this install that restore finds nothing pending (1 strategy, 'No pending strategies to start'), so no effect was observed.
evidence: log/openalgo_2026-11-04.log 08:50:28: 'Successfully loaded 164011 symbols into cache' then 'Error loading symbols to cache: NoneType has no attribute emit' then 'Error in master contract cache hook' (4 ms later, same cause); the catch-up tasks, 'Master contract download completed and confirmed ... 164011 symbols' and 'Auto-login successful' follow at 08:50:28-29. 56 records in log/errors.jsonl = 28 events x 2 records, 10-27 to 11-04. Main logs 10-21 to 11-04: 57 cache loads, 36 with the error, and each of the 36 has openalgoscheduler lines within 90 s; of the 21 without the error, 20 show the Python strategy restore line and the other (11-02 08:46:08) has the error 1 s later. In 35 of the 36 failing loads there is no Python strategy restore line within 30 s.
logs-2026-11-04.md: recurring x4 from 01:21:14 database.master_contract_cache_hook: Error loading symbols to cache: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'emit'
bugs.root_cause: The scheduler 'startup' is a short-lived CLI process. It imports extensions.socketio, a SerializedSocketIO that was never bound to a Flask app (socketio.init_app is only called in app.py:180), so socketio.server is None and emit() raises AttributeError. database/master_contract_cache_hook.py:55 emits unguarded after the cache load has succeeded; the except block at line 86 emits again unguarded, so the second exception escapes load_symbols_to_cache, is caught at hook_into_master_contract_download line 119, and skips the Python strategy restore that follows (lines 106-114). Not an init race or shutdown race: deterministic for every download run from the scheduler process. Same defect class as the 2026-09-29 Flattrade failure, fixed in signal_engine/scripts/openalgoscheduler.py _detach_serverless_socketio (commit 1507b167a) for broker.<name>.database.master_contract_db only, which guards with 'if socketio'. The cache hook imports the same object and was missed. Note the hook has no 'if socketio' guard, so setting its module attribute to None would raise the same error. The fix lives in OpenAlgo core (needs owner approval and a line in docs/strategy-pnl-fork-modification.md) or in a scheduler-side stub with a no-op emit().
bugs.fix: database/master_contract_cache_hook.py (core, uncommitted): _notify_browser skips the cache_loaded emit when socketio.server is None and swallows any other emit failure with logger.exception, at all three emit sites; hook_into_master_contract_download no longer starts the Python strategy restore from a process with no Socket.IO server. Why that last part: with the false error gone the restore would now import blueprints.python_strategy inside the short-lived scheduler CLI, which starts a second APScheduler and could launch strategy processes there; before the fix the restore never ran there, so this keeps that behaviour and the question stays a separate decision. In the app (server bound) browser notifications are unchanged and a failed emit cannot block the restore. Tests: test/test_master_contract_cache_hook_socketio.py 7, test_gthread_core_mode_and_cache_routes + test_gthread_integration 20, session/cache tests 12. Line added to docs/strategy-pnl-fork-modification.md. Full gthread suite run (see report).

bugs.title: Time exit gives up on CGPOWER after 3 attempts, clears both tracker legs and writes no closing row
bugs.plain: When the 14:45 exit order timed out, the engine stopped trying, cleared its records for the position and wrote no closing trade.
bugs.impact: CGPOWER (BREAKINGTRADE and BREAKINGTRADE-RI) had no closing row and no confirmed exit; the sandbox square-off at 15:15 then failed with 'Missing required field: quantity'. The sandbox ended flat, but I did not find which path closed it.

bugs.root_cause: Not confirmed. A human should trace what closed the position, why the tracker cleared the legs after a failed close, and why the square-off lost the quantity.
bugs.fix: signal_engine/tracker.py, signal_engine/main.py (uncommitted). After an independent Opus review the first version was tightened. (1) _own_close_qty excludes another leg's uncertain exit from the 'others' count ONLY when the order book shows that exit order COMPLETE (new _uncertain_exit_filled); an exit still working or not on the book keeps the old count, so a sibling whose stop just filled cannot sell the first leg's shares and reverse the position. (2) _book_one_time_exit returns early for a position the broker still holds: it stays tracked, no close row, no trade counted, no 'closed' message, and is flagged time_exit_left_open; the no-progress exit (tracker._check_no_progress) and a signal EXIT (main._handle_exit_locked) skip a flagged leg, so no second unchecked exit is sent. Dead branches removed. Tests: signal_engine/tests/test_time_exit_uncertain_leg.py 13 (includes the still-working, opposite-direction, no-progress and signal-exit cases), 273 targeted tracker, time-exit, exit-recovery and no-progress tests pass. Old: second leg sent nothing, both legs deleted with the broker still holding the shares. New: second leg sold when its sibling's exit is proven filled; a leg the broker still holds stays tracked and is not exited again on its own. Not changed: the cancelled stop is not re-placed, so a kept leg stays without a stop until it is closed by hand or by the broker square-off (a critical alert is already sent).

bugs.title: A timed-out exit is resent while the first copy is still being processed, so one exit fills three times (AXISBANK 154 sold as 462)
bugs.plain: When the broker was slow, the system sold the same AXISBANK position three times. It briefly ended up 308 shares short, then bought them back about two minutes later.
bugs.impact: A trader briefly held a short position they never intended (308 AXISBANK for roughly 100 seconds, corrected by a duplicate-closing BUY at 13:55:16). Net flat afterwards, so the loss is slippage and charges, but a larger stall or a missed correction would leave a reversed position.
evidence: signal_engine_analyze_2026-11-04.log: 13:50:38 EXIT AXISBANK 154; 13:50:59 attempt 1/3 'Timeout sending order'; 13:51:05 'book is clean: watching 93s for a late fill before any resend'; 13:53:05 attempt 2/3 timeout; 13:53:33 attempt 3/3 timeout; 13:53:37 confirmed id=26110450012762; 13:55:16 CRITICAL 'broker holds extra completed copies (extra: 26110450104136, 26110450103046)'; 13:55:16 'closed the duplicate 308 with BUY id=26110450116202'. Core log: place_order AXISBANK took 168,099 ms (done 13:53:32) and 88,157 ms (done 13:55:03), price stage 167,987 ms and 87,969 ms.
bugs.root_cause: The core inserts a sandbox order only after its price lookup returns, so while the lookup hangs (BUG-007, up to 354 s today) the order is not on the book and a read of the book is clean. The engine's late-fill window (about 93 s, signal_engine/main.py _watch_exit_for_late_fill) is shorter than the stall (168 s here), so it treats the exit as absent and resends; every copy then runs once the lookup returns. The existing duplicate detector and correcting BUY worked, which bounded the damage. No window length fixes this: today's stalls ran from 20 s to 354 s. Options, all execution semantics and not implemented: (a) keep waiting longer before any resend, at the cost of up to that long unprotected (the stop is already cancelled); (b) the core refuses a second order for the same symbol, side, quantity and strategy while one is still in flight, which is a core change; (c) remove the stall for exits by pricing a MARKET exit that reduces a held position without a live quote (core change, also fixes BUG-007).
